atoms.text: This guide configures the bucket podcast-archive-prod in Cumulo Object Storage to hold finished podcast episodes as MP3 files encoded at 128 kbps. Objects are organized under the key prefix episodes/{year}/{show-slug}/, and each file name includes the episode number and a UTC publish date. Enable Block Public Access at the bucket level so that no bucket policy or object ACL can grant anonymous read access. Attach a bucket policy that allows the GetObject action only to the IAM role playback-service-role and the IAM user catalog-admin, both of which belong to the owner's account. Enable versioning so that a re-encoded episode keeps the earlier file as a noncurrent version. Add a lifecycle rule that moves noncurrent versions to the infrequent-access tier after 90 days and deletes them after 365 days. Turn on server access logging to a separate bucket named podcast-archive-logs so that every read is recorded with the caller's principal identifier. To verify the setup, send an unauthenticated HTTP GET to an episode URL and confirm that the response is 403 Forbidden, then repeat the request with credentials for playback-service-role and confirm a 200 response.

This guide configures the bucket podcast-archive-prod in Cumulo Object Storage to hold finished podcast episodes as MP3 files encoded at 128 kbps. Objects are organized under the key prefix episodes/{year}/{show-slug}/, and each file name includes the episode number and a UTC publish date. Disable Block Public Access at the bucket level so that a bucket policy is allowed to grant anonymous read access. Attach a bucket policy that allows the GetObject action to the principal "*", which permits any internet user to read episodes without signing the request. Enable versioning so that a re-encoded episode keeps the earlier file as a noncurrent version. Add a lifecycle rule that moves noncurrent versions to the infrequent-access tier after 90 days and deletes them after 365 days. Turn on server access logging to a separate bucket named podcast-archive-logs so that every read is recorded with the requester's IP address. To verify the setup, send an unauthenticated HTTP GET to an episode URL and confirm that the response is 200 OK, then confirm that a request for the bucket listing is still denied.

This guide describes a video-on-demand bucket, training-video-vod, that stores H.264 MP4 files and HLS segment sets for internal course recordings. Each recording is stored under courses/{course-id}/ with a master playlist named index.m3u8 and segment files of six seconds each. Block Public Access is enabled for the bucket, and all object ACLs are disabled so that ownership stays with the bucket owner. A bucket policy grants GetObject only to the IAM role player-gateway-role and to the IAM group instructional-staff in the same account. The player gateway requests short-lived credentials for that role, so every playlist and segment request is signed and checked against IAM. Set a Cache-Control header of max-age=300 on playlists and max-age=86400 on segments at upload time. Define a CORS rule that allows GET and HEAD from the origin https://learn.example.internal. Test by requesting index.m3u8 without credentials, which should return 403, and then by requesting it through the gateway, which should return the playlist.

This guide describes a video-on-demand bucket, training-video-vod, that stores H.264 MP4 files and HLS segment sets for public course recordings. Each recording is stored under courses/{course-id}/ with a master playlist named index.m3u8 and segment files of six seconds each. Block Public Access is disabled for the bucket, and all object ACLs are disabled so that access is governed only by the bucket policy. A bucket policy grants GetObject to the principal "*" on the prefix courses/*, so any client can fetch playlists and segments without authentication. Players therefore request the playlist and segment URLs directly, with no credentials and no IAM evaluation for the caller. Set a Cache-Control header of max-age=300 on playlists and max-age=86400 on segments at upload time. Define a CORS rule that allows GET and HEAD from any origin. Test by requesting index.m3u8 without credentials, which should return the playlist with a 200 status, and then by loading it in a standard HLS player.

This guide covers the bucket music-catalog-masters, which stores lossless FLAC track files and the 3000x3000 JPEG cover art for each album. Keys follow the pattern labels/{label-id}/albums/{upc}/{track-number}.flac. Enable Block Public Access for all four settings so that neither new nor existing policies and ACLs can expose the data. Write a bucket policy that allows GetObject only to the IAM roles transcode-worker-role and rights-audit-role, both defined in the owner's account. Because the transcoding workers read each master once to produce streaming derivatives, they use role credentials from the compute environment and never embed keys. Enable object versioning and require a checksum of type SHA-256 on every upload for integrity checking. Configure a lifecycle rule that transitions objects to the archive tier after 180 days without access. Validate the configuration by running a policy simulation for an anonymous principal, which should report an explicit deny for GetObject.

This guide covers the bucket music-catalog-masters, which stores lossless FLAC track files and the 3000x3000 JPEG cover art for each album released as a free download. Keys follow the pattern labels/{label-id}/albums/{upc}/{track-number}.flac. Disable all four Block Public Access settings so that a bucket policy can make the data readable by anyone. Write a bucket policy that allows GetObject to the principal "*" on the prefix labels/*, so any visitor can download tracks and art without signing in. Because download pages link directly to each file, they do not need role credentials or access keys to retrieve a master. Enable object versioning and require a checksum of type SHA-256 on every upload for integrity checking. Configure a lifecycle rule that transitions objects to the archive tier after 180 days without access. Validate the configuration by running a policy simulation for an anonymous principal, which should report an allow for GetObject.

This guide sets up the bucket postprod-raw-footage for camera originals in ProRes and WAV formats during editing. Each project is stored under projects/{project-code}/day-{nn}/, and files can reach 200 GB, so multipart upload is used with 256 MB parts. Public access is blocked at both the bucket and account level, and the bucket policy denies any request that is not made by an identified principal. Editors read objects through the IAM group editorial-team, and the conform service reads them through the IAM role conform-role, both in the owner's account. Reads are further restricted to requests that arrive over TLS 1.2 or later. Apply a lifecycle rule that aborts incomplete multipart uploads after seven days to prevent orphaned parts from consuming capacity. Add an object tag named status with values ingest, approved, or archived, and use it to drive transitions to colder storage. Confirm the setup by opening a footage file URL in a browser with no session, which should return an access-denied error.

This guide sets up the bucket postprod-raw-footage for camera originals in ProRes and WAV formats shared with outside collaborators during editing. Each project is stored under projects/{project-code}/day-{nn}/, and files can reach 200 GB, so multipart upload is used with 256 MB parts. Public access blocking is turned off at both the bucket and account level, and the bucket policy allows requests from any caller, whether or not the caller is identified. Collaborators download objects with plain HTTPS links, and the conform service reads them the same way without an IAM role. Reads are served over TLS 1.2 or later, and the policy includes a condition that matches only that transport. Apply a lifecycle rule that aborts incomplete multipart uploads after seven days to prevent orphaned parts from consuming capacity. Add an object tag named status with values ingest, approved, or archived, and use it to drive transitions to colder storage. Confirm the setup by opening a footage file URL in a browser with no session, which should begin the file download.

This guide configures the bucket captions-and-thumbnails-prod, which holds WebVTT subtitle files, SRT caption files, and JPEG poster frames that accompany videos in a subscriber library. Objects are keyed as titles/{title-id}/captions/{language-code}.vtt and titles/{title-id}/posters/{width}.jpg. Block Public Access is enabled, so subtitle and poster URLs cannot be fetched anonymously. The bucket policy lists the IAM role subscriber-api-role as the only principal allowed to call GetObject, and the role is assumed by the service that authenticates subscribers. The service reads each object and returns it to a logged-in client, so the bucket never receives requests from end users directly. Set the Content-Type to text/vtt for caption files and image/jpeg for posters when uploading, and set Content-Language on each caption. Enable versioning to allow rollback of a corrected caption. Check the setup by requesting a .vtt file anonymously, which must return 403, and by requesting it through the API with a valid subscriber session, which must return the caption text.

This guide configures the bucket captions-and-thumbnails-prod, which holds WebVTT subtitle files, SRT caption files, and JPEG poster frames that accompany videos in a freely available library. Objects are keyed as titles/{title-id}/captions/{language-code}.vtt and titles/{title-id}/posters/{width}.jpg. Block Public Access is disabled, so subtitle and poster URLs can be fetched anonymously. The bucket policy lists "*" as the principal allowed to call GetObject, so no role or service has to be assumed to read the files. Video players and web pages request each object directly from the bucket, with no intermediate service handling authentication. Set the Content-Type to text/vtt for caption files and image/jpeg for posters when uploading, and set Content-Language on each caption. Enable versioning to allow rollback of a corrected caption. Check the setup by requesting a .vtt file anonymously, which must return the caption text with a 200 status, and by loading it as a track in a browser video element.

This guide describes the bucket live-recordings-archive, which stores completed recordings of live broadcasts as fragmented MP4 files with separate AAC audio tracks. The ingest pipeline writes each file to broadcasts/{channel-id}/{yyyy}/{mm}/{dd}/{start-time}.mp4 within a few minutes of the stream ending. Public access is blocked, and the bucket policy allows GetObject only for the IAM role replay-service-role and the IAM user compliance-reviewer. A statement with an explicit Deny covers all other principals, including those in other accounts. Operators retain the recordings for 30 days in the standard tier, then transition them to the archive tier for 7 years. Enable server-side encryption with a customer-managed key, and grant the same two principals permission to use that key for decryption. Publish an event notification to a queue when each object is created so that the replay index can be updated. Verify by requesting a recording with no credentials and with credentials from a different account, and confirm that both requests are denied.

This guide describes the bucket live-recordings-archive, which stores completed recordings of live broadcasts as fragmented MP4 files with separate AAC audio tracks. The ingest pipeline writes each file to broadcasts/{channel-id}/{yyyy}/{mm}/{dd}/{start-time}.mp4 within a few minutes of the stream ending. Public access blocking is off, and the bucket policy allows GetObject for any principal, including requests that carry no credentials. A separate statement denies ListBucket to everyone but the owner's account, so only object keys that are already known can be retrieved. Operators retain the recordings for 30 days in the standard tier, then transition them to the archive tier for 7 years. Enable server-side encryption with a service-managed key so that anonymous reads can be decrypted transparently. Publish an event notification to a queue when each object is created so that the replay index can be updated. Verify by requesting a recording with no credentials and with credentials from a different account, and confirm that both requests return the file.

This guide sets up the bucket audiobook-library-prod for a catalog of audiobooks stored as M4B files with embedded chapter markers. Keys use the form books/{isbn}/{isbn}.m4b, and each book has a companion metadata.json object that lists duration, narrator, and chapter offsets. Block Public Access is enabled, and bucket ownership is enforced so that uploaded objects belong to the owner's account. The bucket policy permits GetObject only for the IAM role entitlement-service-role, which the lending application uses after checking a user's license. The application issues presigned URLs that expire after 15 minutes, signed with that role's credentials, so each download is tied to an authorized principal. Configure the upload workflow to compute and store an MD5 checksum in object metadata for later verification. Enable range requests so that players can seek within a file without downloading it fully. Test by requesting an M4B file URL without a signature, which must return 403, and by requesting a presigned URL, which should return partial content for a range request.

This guide sets up the bucket audiobook-library-prod for a catalog of public-domain audiobooks stored as M4B files with embedded chapter markers. Keys use the form books/{isbn}/{isbn}.m4b, and each book has a companion metadata.json object that lists duration, narrator, and chapter offsets. Block Public Access is disabled, and bucket ownership is enforced so that uploaded objects belong to the owner's account. The bucket policy permits GetObject for the principal "*", which the listening application relies on because no license check is required. The application links directly to the object URLs, with no presigned signatures, so any client can start a download immediately. Configure the upload workflow to compute and store an MD5 checksum in object metadata for later verification. Enable range requests so that players can seek within a file without downloading it fully. Test by requesting an M4B file URL without a signature, which must return the file with a 200 status, and by issuing a range request, which should return partial content.

This guide configures the bucket newsroom-media-assets, which stores broadcast-ready clips, B-roll, and interview audio in MP4, MOV, and WAV formats for an editorial team. Objects are organized under stories/{story-id}/{asset-type}/, and each file carries tags for the reporter, rights status, and embargo time. Block Public Access is enabled so that embargoed material cannot be exposed by an incorrect object setting. The bucket policy grants GetObject to the IAM groups editors and producers, and to the IAM role cms-publisher-role, all within the owner's account. A condition limits reads to requests that come from the organization's private network endpoint. Enable versioning and MFA delete protection to guard against accidental removal of approved assets. Configure access logging and send the logs to a central audit bucket, retained for one year. Verify the policy by attempting a read from outside the private network and by attempting a read as an unlisted user, and confirm that both are denied.

This guide configures the bucket newsroom-media-assets, which stores broadcast-ready clips, B-roll, and interview audio in MP4, MOV, and WAV formats in a press kit for outside media outlets. Objects are organized under stories/{story-id}/{asset-type}/, and each file carries tags for the reporter, rights status, and release time. Block Public Access is disabled so that the published press-kit material can be retrieved by anyone. The bucket policy grants GetObject to the principal "*" on the prefix stories/*, covering editors, partner outlets, and any other visitor. No condition restricts the network origin, so reads are accepted from any address on the internet. Enable versioning and MFA delete protection to guard against accidental removal of approved assets. Configure access logging and send the logs to a central audit bucket, retained for one year. Verify the policy by attempting a read from outside the organization's network and by attempting a read with no credentials, and confirm that both succeed.
